BitMine’s $10B unrealized loss sparks debate | SEC annual report uses a different accounting basis | Wait for confirmation at 1,720 before betting on an ETH rebound

My view is to verify the unrealized loss figure first, then assess ETH trading opportunities. Binance Square is discussing #BitMineFaces$10.1BUnrealizedETHLoss. The $10.1 billion figure in the hashtag looks alarming, but it should not be directly presented as BitMine’s latest loss disclosed to the SEC. The company’s 2026 fiscal year 10-K, covering the period through August 31, reports about $6.2291 billion in unrealized losses on digital assets, primarily due to changes in the price of ETH. This is a non-cash fair-value loss for a specific accounting period—not a cash loss from selling today, and not $10.1 billion. The estimate in the viral post must be distinguished from the figure in the financial statements, which uses a different accounting basis.

Now consider the press release the company filed with its November 16 8-K: as of the afternoon of November 15, it held 6,077,745 ETH, using a price of $1,823 per coin at the time; 5,227,037 of those ETH were staked. The company also said it bought 7,653 ETH the previous week. Staked coins are included in total holdings and should not be added again; nor should the company chairman’s optimistic market outlook be treated as a gain already realized. If the trending $10.1 billion figure is an instantaneous estimate based on subtracting the current price from historical cost, the cost basis, holdings date, and price source used must be disclosed. I did not see an amount exactly matching the hashtag in the SEC filings cited above, so I would not treat it as the latest audited figure.

Why does this matter for ETH? The more concentrated a company’s holdings are, the greater the impact of an ETH decline on its income statement and stock valuation, and the more the market may worry about future financing or asset sales. But a book loss does not automatically trigger on-chain liquidations, nor does it mean the company is selling 6.07 million ETH on the market today. Staked holdings generate yield, but also involve lockup arrangements, operational risks, and custody risks, so nominal holdings alone do not tell the whole story. Institutional flows should also be compared with ETFs: Farside’s November 20 ETH fund table provisionally shows $13.2 million in outflows, but ETHA, ETHB, and FETH are all blank, so the total should not be treated as a final, complete picture of institutional flows.

The market’s actual reaction has not been uniformly fearful. A check of Binance ETH/USDT showed a price of around $1,661, with a rolling 24-hour low of $1,544.96 and high of $1,716.58, up about 6.3% from the opening reference price. The rebound from the low has already happened, but the price remains below $1,720. My short-term view is that the recovery is not yet confirmed: holding above $1,650 would create the conditions for another test of $1,720; if the price breaks through and then successfully retests that level, the next target would be $1,760. A renewed drop below $1,600 that cannot be recovered would invalidate the recovery thesis; a break below $1,545 would require reassessing the previous low. A trending figure cannot replace verifiable data.

If I were trading this myself, I would stay out for now and only consider a small long position in spot ETH. The entry trigger would be a move above $1,720 followed by a retest that holds between $1,700 and $1,720, while BTC is no longer falling sharply. I would remain in cash until that trigger occurs. After entry, the position would be capped at 2% of total capital; I would take half off at the first target of $1,760 and hold the rest for $1,820. If the price falls back below $1,700, I would close the remaining position; the hard stop would be below $1,650. I would size the position according to the actual entry price, limit planned loss on any single trade to no more than 0.4% of total capital, and avoid high leverage. I will update my financial assessment when the company makes its next disclosure, and will not treat online estimates as facts from a newly published financial report. #BitMineFaces$10.1BUnrealizedETHLoss #ETH
The above is only my personal market observation and does not constitute investment advice.

BitMine百亿美元浮亏热议｜SEC年报口径不同｜ETH反弹先等1720确认

我的态度是先把浮亏数字核实，再判断ETH的交易机会。币安广场正在讨论#BitMineFaces$10.1BUnrealizedETHLoss，标签里的101亿美元看起来很吓人，但不能直接写成BitMine已向SEC披露的最新亏损。公司提交的2026财年10-K截至8月31日，数字资产未实现损失约62.291亿美元，其中主要来自ETH价格变化；它是特定会计期间的非现金公允价值损益，不是今天卖出兑现的现金亏损，也不是101亿美元。热帖估算与财报数字须分清口径。

再看公司11月16日随8-K提交的新闻稿：截至11月15日下午，其持有6077745枚ETH，当时采用每枚1823美元的报价；其中5227037枚处于质押状态。公司还称前一周买入7653枚ETH。质押币已含在总持仓，不能重复相加；也不能把公司主席对市场的乐观判断当作已经实现的收益。热榜的101亿美元若来自用历史成本与现价相减的即时估算，就必须公开所用成本、持仓时点和价格来源；我在上述SEC文件中没看到与标签完全一致的已披露金额，因此不把它当成审计确认的最新数值。

为什么这事影响ETH？企业持币越集中，ETH下跌对其利润表和股票估值的冲击越大，市场会担心未来融资或资产处置；但账面损失本身并不自动触发链上清算，也不等于公司今天向市场抛售607万枚ETH。质押部分会产生收益，同时存在锁定安排、运营和托管风险，不能只看名义持仓。机构资金还要对照ETF：Farside的11月20日ETH基金表格暂列流出1320万美元，但ETHA、ETHB、FETH均空白，合计不能当作最终完整的机构资金结论。

市场实际反应并非单向恐慌。币安ETH/USDT核对时约1661美元，滚动24小时低1544.96、高1716.58，较开盘参考上涨约6.3%；从低位回升已经发生，却仍在1720下方。我的短线判断是修复尚未确认：1650守住才有继续测试1720的条件，若突破并回踩成功再看1760。若重新跌破1600且无法收复，就推翻修复假设；跌破1545则需要重新评估前低。热榜数字不能代替可核实数据。

如果是我自己交易，目前不参与，方向只预设ETH现货轻仓做多。入场触发是站上1720后回踩1700至1720仍稳住，同时BTC不再急跌；触发前空仓。入场后仓位最多总资金2%，第一目标1760减仓一半，余仓看1820；若回落失守1700先平掉余仓，硬止损参考1650下方。按实际入场价缩小仓位，单笔计划亏损不超过总资金0.4%，不碰高杠杆。待下一份公司披露再更新财务判断，不把网传估算当作已发生的新财报事实。#BitMineFaces$10.1BUnrealizedETHLoss #ETH
以上仅为个人市场观察，不构成投资建议。
